title: Painting the walls without wasting paint
target: How wall painting works in Supermarket Simulator: the bucket as a placed object rather than a resource, the colour carried by that bucket, the wall as something paintable in its own right, and the records the game keeps of what was painted.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with at least one wall you own
Enough money for a bucket and its colour
Somewhere to put the bucket while you work

steps.do: Buy the paint as a bucket rather than as a pot of paint.
steps.because: the paint is an object with its own data behind it, so what you buy is a thing you place and use (PaintBucket, BucketSo)

steps.do: Place the bucket before you expect to paint anything.
steps.because: putting a bucket down is a mode of its own, which is how the game knows a bucket is in use rather than only owned (BucketPlacingMode)

steps.do: Choose the colour on the bucket.
steps.because: a bucket carries colour data, so the colour belongs to the object being used rather than to the wall (ColorData, BucketData)

steps.do: Treat the wall as a paintable object in its own right.
steps.because: walls are their own kind of surface in the game, which is why painting them is separate from painting a floor (PaintableWall)

steps.do: Expect what you painted to be recorded apart from the bucket.
steps.because: the paint has its own data and the system keeps its own save records, so the wall remembers its finish after the bucket is gone (PaintData, BucketSaveData)

steps.do: Expect the whole wall to be one job rather than a patch at a time.
steps.because: a wall is a paintable surface rather than a grid of tiles, so a wall is finished as a wall (PaintableWall)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect everyone to see the same bucket.
steps.because: the bucket has a networked form, so what one player places is placed for the crew (NetworkPaintBucket)

steps.do: Expect the surface to move with the paint rather than only change colour.
steps.because: the painting system carries a wobble of its own, so the finish is animated rather than a flat fill (Wobble)

steps.do: Do not treat a repaint as free just because the wall is already painted.
steps.because: repainting has data of its own rather than being the same as painting a bare wall (RepaintData)

commonMistakes: Looking for paint as a resource in the stock list instead of buying a bucket.
Choosing a colour and expecting it to apply to every wall at once.
Repainting a wall and expecting the old finish to be replaced without being recorded.
Painting in a shared shop without checking that everyone else can see the bucket.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
